clinicalPearls: A severe autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic mutations in LAMB2, the gene encoding the laminin beta-2 chain.
Classically combines congenital nephrotic syndrome with distinctive ocular anomalies, most notably fixed narrow pupils (microcoria).
Kidney disease usually manifests as congenital or early infantile nephrotic syndrome with diffuse mesangial sclerosis on biopsy.
Ocular features extend beyond microcoria to include lens and retinal abnormalities and later visual impairment.
Neurodevelopmental delay and hypotonia are frequent, partly reflecting laminin beta-2 expression at the neuromuscular junction and in the central nervous system.
Milder LAMB2 variants can produce attenuated phenotypes with later-onset proteinuria and subtler eye findings.
Renal failure typically develops in infancy or early childhood, often requiring dialysis and transplantation.
Genetic confirmation of biallelic LAMB2 mutations establishes the diagnosis and enables family counselling.
reference.pathophysiology: Pierson syndrome arises from loss-of-function mutations in LAMB2, which encodes the laminin beta-2 chain, a component of laminin-521 and related heterotrimers that are critical structural elements of several specialised basement membranes. Laminin beta-2 is highly expressed in the glomerular basement membrane, where it anchors podocytes and maintains the integrity of the filtration barrier; its deficiency destabilises this barrier and produces congenital nephrotic syndrome with the histological pattern of diffuse mesangial sclerosis. The same laminin chain is essential in the intraocular basement membranes and in the developing pupil and lens, so its absence causes microcoria and other ocular malformations, and it is a key element of the synaptic basement membrane at the neuromuscular junction and within parts of the nervous system, accounting for the hypotonia and neurodevelopmental impairment. The severity of the phenotype broadly tracks the degree of residual laminin beta-2 function, with complete loss producing the full classic triad in early infancy and hypomorphic variants yielding milder, later-onset renal and ocular disease.
additionalDifferentials: Congenital nephrotic syndrome of the Finnish type (NPHS1 mutations)
Denys-Drash syndrome (WT1 mutations with diffuse mesangial sclerosis and genital anomalies)
Galloway-Mowat syndrome (nephrosis with microcephaly and neurological features)
Other podocyte gene disorders such as NPHS2-related nephrotic syndrome
Congenital infections causing nephrotic syndrome in infancy
additionalInvestigations: Molecular genetic testing for biallelic LAMB2 mutations
Renal biopsy demonstrating diffuse mesangial sclerosis where performed
Quantification of proteinuria and serum albumin
Detailed ophthalmological examination for microcoria, lens and retinal anomalies
Neurodevelopmental assessment and cranial imaging where indicated
Renal function monitoring for progression to kidney failure
Parental carrier testing and genetic counselling
redFlags: Congenital or early infantile nephrotic syndrome with severe hypoalbuminaemia and oedema
Fixed narrow pupils or other structural eye anomalies in an infant with proteinuria
Rapid progression to kidney failure in infancy
Complications of severe nephrotic syndrome such as thrombosis or infection
reference.prognosis: Classic Pierson syndrome carries a poor prognosis, with early progression to kidney failure and significant ocular and neurological morbidity, and some infants do not survive early childhood. Milder LAMB2 phenotypes have a more variable, less severe course.
pitfalls: Attributing congenital nephrotic syndrome solely to NPHS1 or WT1 and overlooking LAMB2
Missing microcoria or other ocular signs that point to the specific diagnosis
Assuming immunosuppression will control a genetically determined nephrotic syndrome
Underestimating the neurological component and its impact on development
Failing to offer genetic counselling and carrier testing to families
references: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics (standard reference)
